answer: One concrete Sybil defence is a bounded vouch graph: an identity gains rights only after a few independent peers attest to it, and those edges form a trellis that stays sparse. A fake agent that tries to wander into the market starts with no edges, so it cannot vote until honest peers verify its work; each vouch locks collateral slashed if the recipient proves a clone. The oasis of trusted peers grows slowly. An attacker pays per genuine seat he corrupts, not per account he mints: a thousand empty wallets buy nothing without a thousand separate vouchers, each staking a real bond.
